title: Vietnam vs Cambodia: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Vietnam and Cambodia based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 🍜 Food & Dining
categories.summary: Vietnam is, simply put, one of the best food countries on the planet. Every region has its own distinct cuisine: Hanoi's phở bò (beef pho) and bún chả, Huế's bún bò Huế and bánh bèo, Hội An's cao lầu and white rose dumplings, and Ho Chi Minh City's bánh mì and cơm tấm (broken rice). redditQuotes: I've been to both and loved Vietnam so much, we visited twice. Better food. The caves in Phong Nha were gorgeous! Loved Hanoi, Hoi An, Hue, and Saigon as well."—r/travel user

categories.title: 🏛️ Temples, History & Culture
categories.summary: This is Cambodia's knockout category. Angkor Wat is not just a temple — it's the largest religious monument on Earth, a 162.6-hectare complex that was the center of the Khmer Empire. categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Both countries are extremely affordable by global standards, but Vietnam edges ahead as the cheaper option — especially for daily food and transport. Cambodia's quirk is its dual-currency system: US dollars are used everywhere alongside Cambodian riel (KHR), and tourist-facing prices tend to be in U
redditQuotes: Vietnam is a lot more developed, better food, more cities to visit, different climates, and is cleaner in general."—r/cambodia user

categories.title: 🛵 Getting Around
categories.summary: Vietnam has significantly better transport infrastructure. The Grab app (Southeast Asia's Uber) works seamlessly in all major Vietnamese cities — motorbike taxis for $1–3 across town, cars for $3–8. redditQuotes: Vietnam and Cambodia aren't as easy to city hop as places like Western Europe. You're going to burn through too much time traveling between places."—r/travel user

categories.title: ☀️ Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Cambodia has a simple weather story: dry season (November–April) and wet season (May–October). The sweet spot isNovember to February— temperatures hover around 25–32°C with low humidity and barely any rain. March and April are brutally hot (regularly 38–42°C). categories.title: 🏨 Where to Stay
categories.summary: Hanoi — Old Quarter— The classic base. Chaotic, atmospheric, walkable. Hundreds of hotels, hostels, and street food within arm's reach. Phở Gia Truyền and Bún Chả Hương Liên (Obama's bún chả spot) are minutes away.

categories.title: 🎒 Day Trips
categories.summary: Vietnam's geographic diversity means each base city unlocks different experiences. Cambodia's day trips are more concentrated but no less impressive.

categories.title: 🔀 Why Not Both?
categories.summary: The most popular multi-country route in Southeast Asia isVietnam + Cambodia, and for good reason. faqs.question: Is Vietnam or Cambodia better for first-time visitors to Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Vietnam is generally recommended for first-timers. It has better tourist infrastructure, more diverse landscapes (mountains, beaches, cities, caves), a wider food scene, and reliable ride-hailing apps like Grab. faqs.question: How much does it cost to travel in Vietnam vs Cambodia per day?
faqs.answer: Vietnam is slightly cheaper overall. Budget travelers spend $25–40/day in Vietnam vs $30–50/day in Cambodia. Mid-range travelers spend $50–80/day in Vietnam vs $60–90/day in Cambodia. faqs.question: Can you combine Vietnam and Cambodia in one trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely, and it's one of the most popular multi-country routes in Southeast Asia. The HCMC → Phnom Penh bus takes 6 hours (~$15). faqs.question: Which country has better food, Vietnam or Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Vietnam, by a wide margin — this is one of the few things Reddit almost universally agrees on. Vietnamese cuisine (phở, bánh mì, bún chả, cơm tấm) is among the world's great food cultures. Cambodia's fish amok and lok lak are excellent, but the depth and variety don't compare. faqs.question: Is Cambodia safe for tourists in 2026?
faqs.answer: Cambodia is generally safe, especially in Siem Reap and Phnom Penh's tourist areas. Standard precautions apply: watch for bag snatching on motorbikes in Phnom Penh, use reputable transport, and avoid flashing valuables. faqs.question: How long do you need in Vietnam vs Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Vietnam rewards extended stays: 2–3 weeks minimum to see the highlights (Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Hoi An, HCMC, Mekong Delta). Cambodia can be covered in 5–7 days: 3 days Siem Reap/Angkor, 2 days Phnom Penh, plus optional beach time on Koh Rong. If you have 10 days total, Vietnam gives you more variety;
